What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

jobs.title: Staff Turbomachinery Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Staff Turbomachinery Engineer to serve as the Responsible Engineer for the turbomachinery within our nuclear-driven power generation system. This role owns the mechanical design, integrity, and performance of the core rotating assembly at the heart of our 1MW closed-loop Brayton cycle.

You will define and drive the mechanical architecture of high-speed rotating hardware operating at extreme temperatures, pressures, and rotational speeds. As a deeply technical individual contributor, you will set direction for rotor dynamics, structures, bearings, seals, and system integration while working closely with electrical, thermal, and manufacturing teams.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role focused on technical excellence, sound engineering judgment, and delivering reliable, production-ready turbomachinery.



Responsibilities & Duties:

Technical Ownership & System Architecture

 - Serve as Responsible Engineer for the turbomachinery mechanical system.

 - Own the mechanical architecture and design strategy for high-speed rotating assemblies (up to ~30 krpm).

 - Lead rotor dynamics, structural integrity, and life analysis for rotating components and assemblies.

 - Define and flow down requirements from system-level constraints including thermal, structural, and operational environments.

 - Make key technical decisions on rotor layout, shafting, bearings, seals, materials, and clearances.

 - Ensure designs meet performance, reliability, safety, and regulatory requirements.

 - Establish and uphold standards for mechanical design rigor, analysis quality, and documentation.

Mechanical Design & Analysis

 - Lead detailed design of turbomachinery components including rotors, shafts, housings, and support structures.

 - Test and validate rotordynamic systems, driving model correlation, risk reduction, and performance verification.

 - Perform and review structural and thermal analysis to ensure integrity under high-speed and high-temperature operation.

 - Define tolerances, fits, stack-ups, and alignment strategies for precision rotating assemblies.

 - Partner with electrical engineering on alternator rotor integration, including electromagnetic and structural coupling.

Cross-Functional Integration

 - Partner closely with turbomachinery aero, motor design, thermal, manufacturing, and test teams.

 - Ensure seamless integration between turbine, compressor, and alternator subsystems.

 - Drive clear interface definitions across mechanical, electrical, and thermal boundaries.

 - Collaborate with manufacturing to ensure designs are producible, inspectable, and scalable.

 - Engage with suppliers on technically critical components and design decisions.

Prototyping, Testing & Validation

 - Support assembly, integration, and test of turbomachinery hardware.

 - Define validation strategies including spin testing, thermal testing, and system-level operation.

 - Lead root cause analysis and drive design iteration for test failures or performance gaps.

 - Remain hands-on in hardware bring-up, troubleshooting, and refinement.

Technical Influence

 - Act as a subject matter expert in turbomachinery mechanical design and rotating systems.

 - Provide technical guidance and design reviews across the team without direct people management responsibility.

 - Influence engineering direction through deep expertise, data-driven decisions, and strong judgment.

 - Contribute to technical roadmap, risk identification, and mitigation strategies.

Required Qualifications & Skills:

 - B.S. in Mechanical Engineering or related field.

 - 8+ years of experience designing high-speed rotating machinery (turbines, compressors, or similar systems).

 - Deep expertise in structural analysis and mechanical design of turbomachinery.

 - Experience with bearings, seals, and high-speed shafting design.

 - Expert-level proficiency with analysis tools (e.g., ANSYS) and advanced use of NX and Teamcenter for complex design, simulation, and product lifecycle management.

 - Strong understanding of tolerancing, GD&T, and precision mechanical assembly.

 - Experience owning hardware through design, build, and test cycles.

 - Hands-on experience with assembly, integration, and troubleshooting of turbomachinery.

 - Strong system-level thinking and mechanical intuition.

 - Excellent engineering judgment and decision-making capability.

 - Ability to influence without authority across cross-functional teams.

 - Clear communicator capable of articulating complex technical concepts.

 - High ownership mindset and accountability for hardware outcomes.

 - Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, first-of-a-kind development environment.

Desired Qualifications & Skills:

 - M.S. or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering.

 - Experience with closed-loop Brayton cycle systems or similar energy systems.

 - Familiarity with high-temperature materials and extreme environment design.

 - Experience integrating mechanical systems with high-speed electric machines.

 - Prior experience as a Responsible Engineer for complex hardware.

 - Experience scaling hardware from prototype to production.

Additional Requirements:

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must work 100% onsite at El Segundo HQ.
   
   


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

jobs.title: Controls Engineer: Power Generation
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design and integrate automation systems for on-site power generation serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement.

Role focus: Control-system architecture, integration, and commissioning for on-site generation

Travel: 50%

Responsibilities

 - Define control-system architecture, functional design specifications, sequences of operation, cause-and-effect matrices, alarm philosophy, and interface requirements.

 - Integrate OEM controls, PLCs, DCS, SCADA, historian, microgrid controllers, protection systems, and data center BMS or EPMS platforms.

 - Develop and review I/O lists, network architecture, control narratives, graphics, alarm limits, interlocks, permissives, and fail-safe behavior.

 - Coordinate synchronization, load sharing, islanding, black start, load shedding, restoration, and generation-to-data-center operating modes.

 - Evaluate cybersecurity, redundancy, time synchronization, communications protocols, data quality, and remote-support requirements.

 - Lead or support software reviews, simulator testing, factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, and tuning.

 - Troubleshoot control-system and plant-performance issues and convert findings into corrective actions and reusable standards.

 - Partner with electrical, mechanical, CSA, IT, security, operations, OEM, EPC, and data center controls teams.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 8+ years of controls, automation, or instrumentation engineering experience in power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure.

 - Strong experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration.

 - Knowledge of generation controls, synchronization, load sharing, protective interfaces, process control, and safety interlocks.

 - Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

 - Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

 - Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices.

 - Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with IEC 61850, Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols.

jobs.title: Data Center Controls Engineer (BMS / EPMS)
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI is building the infrastructure foundation for the next generation of AI. The Data Center Engineering team defines the strategy, reference architectures, technical requirements, and delivery standards for the large-scale data centers that support OpenAI research, products, and infrastructure partners.

As a Data Center Controls Engineer, you will program, configure, integrate, and commission the controls systems that support high-density AI data centers. You will work hands-on with mechanical or electrical controls, partnering with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, security, commissioning, operations, and external delivery teams.

About the Role

We are seeking hands-on, early-career controls engineers with practical experience in building management systems (BMS) and mechanical controls, or electrical power monitoring systems (EPMS) and electrical controls. This role focuses on implementing and commissioning control systems, including PLCs, field devices, instrumentation, and sequences of operation, rather than owning OT/IT network or cybersecurity architecture.

The ideal candidate has day-to-day experience programming and commissioning controls, ideally with a controls systems integrator. We welcome depth in either BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls; expertise in both is not required. You will work with experienced engineers and delivery partners to turn design requirements into reliable, tested systems.

Key Responsibilities

 - Program and configure PLCs and control systems for mechanical/BMS or electrical/EPMS applications in AI data center campuses.

 - Implement and test sequences of operation, control logic, alarms, and interlocks against approved functional requirements.

 - Review and maintain controls documentation, including control diagrams, I/O and point lists, instrumentation details, sequences of operation, and commissioning records.

 - Integrate field devices, sensors, instrumentation, equipment controllers, and supervisory systems; validate point mapping, communications, and data quality.

 - Maintain control programs, configuration backups, version history, change records, and rollback procedures to support safe commissioning and operations.

 - Partner with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, cybersecurity, and operations teams to resolve integration issues and implement approved OT connectivity and security requirements.

 - Configure and troubleshoot relevant industrial communications, such as BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, or IEC 61850, according to the system and controls discipline.

 - Work directly with controls integrators, equipment vendors, contractors, and commissioning teams to resolve programming, installation, and functional performance issues.

 - Execute and document factory and site acceptance testing, point-to-point checks, sequence verification, and integrated systems testing; troubleshoot control logic, instrumentation, alarms, and device communication failures.

Qualifications

 - Practical hands-on experience programming, configuring, integrating, or commissioning control systems in data centers, industrial automation, buildings, or other critical infrastructure environments.

 - Working knowledge of PLC programming and control logic, with the ability to implement and troubleshoot sequences of operation.

 - Experience in either BMS/mechanical controls or EPMS/electrical controls, with an understanding of the equipment and operating sequences in that discipline.

 - Experience configuring field devices and instrumentation, validating I/O and point mapping, and diagnosing control system behavior.

 - Working knowledge of relevant industrial communication protocols and basic OT networking needed to connect and troubleshoot control systems.

 - Ability to read control diagrams, equipment documentation, I/O lists, and functional specifications, and keep implementation records accurate.

 - Hands-on experience with functional testing, commissioning, and systematic troubleshooting using trends, alarms, logs, and field observations.

 - Ability to work closely with integrators, vendors, construction teams, and operations, communicate issues clearly, and follow safe work and change-control practices.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls or Automation Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience at a controls systems integrator, with regular responsibility for programming, configuration, field integration, and commissioning.

 - Experience delivering BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls for data centers or other mission-critical facilities.

 - Familiarity with supervisory controls, HMI/SCADA configuration, telemetry, and historian integrations.

 - Familiarity with OT cybersecurity practices and working with networking or security specialists to implement approved access and connectivity requirements.

 - Experience with scripting, APIs, or automation tools that improve controls testing, integration, documentation, or troubleshooting.

Work Environment and Travel

 - This role requires periodic travel to data center campuses, vendors, labs, construction sites, commissioning activities, and controls/network cutovers.

 - The engineer should be comfortable working across office, lab, construction, and live data center environments, including PPE, lockout/tagout, cyber hygiene, and change-control requirements.

 - Work may include time-sensitive support during commissioning, startup, vendor testing, cutovers, network changes, telemetry issues, automation failures, and operational events.

Travel: 50%

Department: Catering and Conference Services

Position: Assistant Director of Catering and Conference Services

Reports To: Director of Catering and Conference Services

Position Summary

The Assistant Director of Catering & Conference Services supports the strategic and operational leadership of the Catering and Conference Services Department. This position is responsible for maximizing banquet, catering, meeting, conference, weddings and group event revenues while ensuring an exceptional luxury guest experience. The role assists in leading the planning, coordination, execution, and follow-up of all group meetings, social events, weddings, corporate functions, incentive programs, and special events.

The Assistant Director partners closely with Sales, Food & Beverage, Culinary, Banquets, Revenue Management, Rooms Division, and other operational departments to ensure seamless event execution that reflects the luxury standards and brand values of the resort.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development

• Conduct regular departmental meetings, training sessions, and one-on-one coaching.
• Support recruitment, onboarding, succession planning, and talent development initiatives.

Sales & Revenue Generation

Event Planning & Execution

Financial Management

Operational Excellence

Experience

Success Factors

Compliance and Ethics

• Foster strong working relationships throughout the resort.
• Support cross-functional teamwork and problem-solving.

Operational Excellence

Financial Responsibilities

• Support inventory management and purchasing controls.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Recruiter & Portfolio Owner
jobs.description:
About Agile Defense
 
At Agile Defense we know that action defines the outcome and new challenges require new solutions. That’s why we always look to the future and embrace change with an unmovable spirit and the courage to build for what comes next.
 
Our vision is to bring adaptive innovation to support our nation's most important missions through the seamless integration of advanced technologies, elite minds, and unparalleled agility—leveraging a foundation of speed, flexibility, and ingenuity to strengthen and protect our nation’s vital interests.


Why This Role Exists
Senior Technical Recruiter is where portfolio ownership becomes the job. Agile Defense needs experienced recruiters who can own a full portfolio of technical, cleared requisitions and the senior stakeholders behind them — Program Managers, Directors, Capture leads — end-to-end, while coaching and raising the floor for the Recruiter I's and II's around them.
This is the senior individual-contributor delivery seat on the team: the recruiter other people's hardest searches get routed to, and the proving ground for anyone interested in the operational or people-leadership track that follows — Recruiting Lead or Recruiting Manager.
Performance Objectives — What Success Requires
These are the outcomes that define success in this seat over your first year. They are not a list of duties — they are the results you'll be measured against.
Own a full portfolio of senior stakeholders. Within 90 days, take full ownership of a portfolio of technical, cleared requisitions spanning multiple senior stakeholders (Program Managers, Directors, Capture leads), and become a trusted authority on hiring cleared technical talent up through TS/SCI with polygraph.
Mentor and coach junior recruiters. On an ongoing basis, mentor Recruiter I and II team members, with at least one showing a measurable improvement in independent req ownership, compliance accuracy, or candidate-experience feedback within two quarters of your coaching.
Recommend and contribute to process improvement. Identify at least one process or workflow gap per year and bring a concrete, well-reasoned recommendation to your Recruiting Lead or Manager — with the credibility and data to make the case.
Deliver consistently on the hardest searches. Be a recruiter your Recruiting Lead routes complex or sensitive requisitions to, and deliver strong outcomes on them without needing close oversight.
Model AI-enabled, human-led recruiting. Maintain and refine your own AI-assisted practices, and actively share them with Recruiter I and II teammates — always in service of a better human experience, not a replacement for it.
Champion diverse, qualified slates. Each quarter, partner with at least one senior hiring team to build and present a deliberate strategy for a more diverse, representative finalist slate — without lowering the bar for cleared, technical qualification.
What Success Looks Like
First 90 Days
You've absorbed your portfolio, built credibility with senior stakeholders, and are operating independently across the full complexity range, including TS/SCI and polygraph searches.
First 6 Months
At least one recruiter you're coaching is noticeably more capable than when you started, and you've brought at least one credible process recommendation forward.
First 12 Months
You're a recruiter your Recruiting Lead or Manager routes the hardest, most senior, or most sensitive reqs to — and you're ready to consider whether your next step is deeper portfolio ownership, a Recruiting Lead track leading a program or workstream beyond delivery, or people management.
Your Scope & Environment
You'll report to the VP of Talent Acquisition and own a full portfolio — typically 15-20+ concurrent requisitions — for mid-to-senior technical and programmatic roles, working alongside the Recruiter I/II teammates you help develop and partnering closely with HR, Security/Facility Security Officers (FSO), compensation, and contracts staff.
Expect real ownership of the relationships that matter most to a program's success, and real influence over how the team works — without yet carrying the org-wide program-building, prioritization, or escalation responsibilities that define a Recruiting Lead.
What You Bring
We're not screening for years of experience or a specific past title. We're looking for evidence that you can deliver the objectives above. That typically looks like:
A demonstrated track record independently owning full-cycle recruiting for technical, cleared positions up through TS/SCI with polygraph.
A track record of informally or formally coaching other recruiters and genuinely wanting to see them grow.
Confidence managing multiple senior stakeholders at once, including the ability to push back, advise, and influence a hiring decision when the data says you should.
Experience building or meaningfully improving a process, tool, or workflow, and partnering with hiring managers to make it stick.
A genuine, demonstrable personal interest in applying AI to recruiting work, paired with a firm point of view on where automation belongs and where it doesn't.
A real, lived belief that diverse slates and diverse interview panels produce better hiring outcomes, evidenced by specific outcomes you've driven.
Working knowledge of how federal contract cycles — recompetes, awards, labor categories, staffing plans — shape hiring urgency and timing.
Clearance, Location & Travel
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)  |  Travel: Minimal / occasional (client sites in the US or Reston, VA / McLean, VA & the DMV region) 
Other ideal locations would include Greater Tampa, FL region or Ft. Huachuca, AZ
Clearance: Must be clearable for a U.S. Secret security clearance (minimum)

jobs.title: Claims & Injury Manager
jobs.description:
To oversee and coordinate the claims and injury management function for relevant portfolio. This will include but is not limited to; strategic claims and incident management, ensuring appropriate medical treatment, return to work and all other aspects of injury management and workers compensation services. This will be done in consultation with internal and external stakeholders in a timely manner and in accordance with legislative requirements and Company Policies and Procedures. Will work in close collaboration with the General Manager Workers Compensation & Injury Management in providing leadership to the injury management team to engender a high performance culture and commitment to goal achievement. Based at a Sodexo Support Centre, this role provides support to regional areas and travel may be required.

Job Scope

Ensure Corporate, Legislative and Regulatory obligations are adhered to and breaches reported

to General Manager Workers Compensation & Injury Management

Influence and negotiate with key stakeholders to achieve desired outcomes associated with injury

and illness

Demonstrate leadership to department staff to successfully implement strategies to achieve

improvements and best practice in management of personal injury and illness, cost outcomes

and safety performance.

Responsibilities

Plan, develop and implement pro-active injury management and rehabilitation strategies

Ensure and deliver business support in line with the injury management and fitness for work

framework

Ensure a consistently high standard of injury, claims and people management is maintained in

achievement of departmental and company goals.

Assist with managing change and encourage staff team members to contribute to improvement

initiatives and a continuous improvement philosophy

Communicate, influence and negotiate with key stakeholders to achieve best possible outcomes

and minimise injury and illness costs

Provide analytical reports to leadership and operational teams to assist with incident analysis and

mitigation

Ensure legal compliance with existing and proposed legislation associated with injury

management and fitness for work

Actively participate and take a leadership approach in claim reviews with insurer on a regular

basis

Ensure appropriate escalation and reporting to internal and external stakeholders in required

timeframes

Authorise and process weekly compensation payments ensuring timely reimbursement from

Insurers

Ensure external or outsourced injury management support is kept abreast of internal changes

Support development and delivery of the internal injury management training package ensuring

training presentation is current, sessions planned in advance and attendee records are updated.

Contribute to department planning and budgeting process

Manage claims staffing model including recruitment, retention, training and competency

development to ensure sufficient and appropriate resources to manage the injury management

process and to achieve required outcomes

Encourage, develop and prepare individuals for succession planning and future development

opportunities

Support annual insurance renewals to ensure current workers compensation endorsed policy

certificates are in place.

Proactively encourage an environment of wellbeing across the business

Degree in Allied Health or similar (Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Exercise Physiology, Workplace Health & Safety)

Experiences

Minimum 5 years’ experience in workers compensation claims and injury management

Knowledge & Skills

Comprehensive knowledge of Workers Compensation legislation across all jurisdictions

Experience in team leadership

Experience in workplace training

Knowledge of SolvInjury system

Timely record-keeping skills with attention to detail;

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Excellent analysis, negotiation and decision making skills

Strong initiative and able to work autonomously;

Strong understanding of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook)

Why choose Sodexo?

Sodexo is a people business, employing over 400,000 people worldwide and thousands in Australia. Our employees, who personify Sodexo's unique values of Service Spirit, Team Spirit and Spirit of Progress, are our greatest asset through their commitment and dedication.  Working with Sodexo is more than a job; it’s a chance to be part of something greater because we believe our everyday actions have a big impact. With us, you belong in a company that allows you to act with purpose and thrive in your own way. We are always looking for people to join our team and help us create a lasting impact on individuals, society, and the planet.

At Sodexo, we are a proud Equal Opportunity Employer and encourage applications from all applicants regardless of age, race, sex, ethnicity, religion and beliefs and people with disabilities.

We offer a competitive salary, many development opportunities and an outstanding benefits and recognition program!

jobs.title: Office and Events Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT CLIPBOARD

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.


Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/ and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’ve just moved into a new HQ in downtown San Francisco and are looking for a motivated, high-ownership and creative Office and Events Manager to join our team onsite. This role will be a blend of day-to-day oversight of operations on site for our in-office team as well as support planning and executing regular offsites and events in San Francisco and (at times) around the country.

A non-exhaustive list of what responsibilities day-to-day may include:

 1. Keeping the office stocked with food, drink and other supplies

 2. Managing relationships with F&B, IT and other vendors

 3. Coordinating with our building managers and any repair and maintenance vendors

 4. Supporting on-site contractors or designers as we continue to build out HQ

 5. Handling daily lunch orders for the team (roughly ~20-30 folks onsite on an average day and up 60+ for events and off-sites.

 6. Supporting in logistics and planning for off-sites (typically 1-2 per quarter)

 7. Managing suite and building level guest access


ABOUT THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

You may be a good fit for this role if you are:

 1. High ownership. Nothing slips through the cracks or needs to be chased down.

 2. Proactive. You don’t wait to be told what to do, you spot needs and lead with solutions.

 3. Detail-oriented. You do sweat the small stuff and nothing slips by you.

Job Purpose and Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work.  We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day and our Pharmacy Technicians (Technicians) play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise.

As a Technician, you will support the pharmacy team in delivering operational and service excellence within your store. Technicians are often the first point of contact to assist our patients and customers to deliver an exceptional experience. Technicians assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. Technicians operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout their shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, they demonstrate genuine care and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

Once in role, Technicians are required to complete a rigorous company training program and satisfy all registration, licensing, and certification requirements according to their State’s Board of Pharmacy guidelines. Until the Pharmacy Technician has completed all necessary requirements, duties may be restricted by the Pharmacy Manager.

A Technician is responsible for contributing to safe and effective operations of the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

• Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists manage and improve patient health
• Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
• Contributing to positive patient experiences by showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
• Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
• Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
• Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
• Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
• Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the Pharmacy Technician may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

• Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
• Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
• Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
• Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient
• Monitoring and managing vaccine supplies

As part of the bold vision to deliver the “Next Generation” of managed care in Ohio Medicaid, OhioRISE will help struggling children and their families by focusing on the individual with strong coordination and partnership among MCOs, vendors, and ODM to support specialization in addressing critical needs. o Using holistic approach consults with case managers, supervisors, Medical Directors and/or other health/behavioral health programs to overcome barriers to meeting goals and objectives; presents cases at case conferences to obtain multidisciplinary review in order to achieve optimal outcomes.

o Works collaboratively with the members' Child and Family Teams.

o Identifies and escalates quality of care issues through established channels.

o Utilizes negotiation skills to secure appropriate options and services necessary to meet the member's benefits and/or healthcare needs.

o Utilizes influencing/ motivational interviewing skills to ensure maximum member engagement and promote lifestyle/behavior changes to achieve optimum level of health.

o Provides coaching, information, and support to empower the member to make ongoing independent medical and/or healthy lifestyle choices.

o Helps member actively and knowledgably participate with their provider in healthcare decision-making.

o Serves a single point of contact for members and assist members to remediate immediate and acute gaps in care and access.

• Monitoring, Evaluation and Documentation of Care:

o Utilizes case management and quality management processes in compliance with regulatory and accreditation guidelines and company policies and procedures.

Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Job Purpose and Summary:

The District Pharmacy Coordinator (DPC) plays a critical role supporting the effective coordination of scheduling in pharmacies across their market. With strong organization skills, high accountability, and consistent follow-through, the DPC ensures that all pharmacist schedules are created and published on time, with coverage and contingency plans in-place, to support day-to-day pharmacy operations and protect against business disruption. The DPC additionally supports the scheduling and staffing of outside immunization clinics, supporting client relationships and ensuring clinic teams are prepared for success. The DPC serves as a timekeeping administrator for market pharmacists and is responsible for accurate and timely execution of pharmacist payroll submission. As a key support to the Pharmacy District Leader (Rx DL), the DPC serves as a delegate to execute base changes, track and monitor vacation requests, manage pay code balances and may support additional administrative activities related to the compliant and effective functioning of market pharmacies, including but not limited to:

• Partnering with Rx DL to identify and close any gaps with PIC/POA registrations for each pharmacy location with the state Board of Pharmacy
• Escalating and/or following up on issues impacting effective pharmacy operations, e.g. TempAlert excursions, Service Channel tickets, store supply ordering, exception reporting, audits, etc.

This is a non-exempt, 30-hour per week role; the DPC may choose to work 10 additional hours per week in a local CVS pharmacy as a Technician to augment their pay and stay closer to pharmacy operations in support of enhanced market performance.

Primary Job Duties & Responsibilities:

1. Set and maintain Pharmacist schedule for stores in the district, including creation and maintenance of Pharmacist templates, appropriate scheduling of DSPs, pharmacist vacation coverage, and the maintenance of staffing contingency plans (e.g., active and up-to-date call-list for sick call or other required unplanned coverage). Track pharmacist vacation balances and send regular reporting, reminders, and request to ensure pharmacists are utilizing vacation time, partnering with Rx DL for the timely review and approval of all pharmacist vacation requests. Partner appropriately to ensure any Pharmacists eligible for LOA & RA are supported and scheduled effectively. Strive to utilize pharmacist base hours effectively and partner with the Rx DL for timely review of HUB/HOB use. Escalate any financial risk (e.g. Hours Under Base) for the Rx DL’s attention. -60%

2. Track and submit pharmacist payroll weekly, in accordance with the CVS Pharmacist Payroll Administrative Guide. Enter regular and other applicable non-work time (e.g. vacation, sick, etc.), enter any shift or market-specific requirements (e.g. night rates, predictability pay, etc.), and review for quality assurance prior to submission.  - 10%

3. Seasonally, manage vaccine clinic scheduling, including inputting clinics into the schedule three weeks in advance, checking the scheduling tool daily for additional clinic requests, revising pharmacist schedules to cover clinics, and preventing client escalations through proactive planning and balancing of priorities. Ensure coverage of any pharmacist holes in store schedules created by clinics that store pharmacists have personally secured and plan to staff.  -10%

4. Support additional administrative needs at the direction of the Rx DL to support day-to-day pharmacy operations, key initiatives, pilots and ensure safe, effective, and compliant pharmacy operations, e.g. Workday Delegate tasks/job changes (transfers, base changes), following up on PIC/POA registrations, COEs, TempAlert excursions, Service Channel tickets and escalations, audit remediations, etc. -20%

High School Diploma or General Equivalent Development (GED) - Required

jobs.title: Pharmacy Intern
jobs.description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work.  We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

• Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
• Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
• Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
• Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
• Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
• Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
• Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
• Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
• Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
• Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
• Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

• Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
• Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
• Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
• Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

• Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
• Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

• Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
• Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
• Attention and Focus:Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of timeAbility to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needsAbility to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
• Customer Service and Team Orientation:Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly mannerNotice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
• Communication Skills:Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleaguesUtilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
• Mathematical Reasoning:Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
• Problem Resolution:Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
• Physical Demands:Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of timeLift, scan, and bag itemsReach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp itemsMove fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or armExtend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift itemsControl precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positionsStoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waistClose visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small partsOccasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately; Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
• Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

• 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
• Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
• Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
• Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

Pay Range

$20.50 - $24.25

As health care innovators, we are making quality care affordable, accessible, simple and seamless. jobs.description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work.  We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

• Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
• Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
• Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
• Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
• Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
• Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
• Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
• Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
• Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
• Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
• Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

• Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
• Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
• Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
• Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

• Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Meet the Team

Our innovations in silicon, optics, and hardware platforms are shaping the technology industry. We're a global team of creative experts, bringing our unique backgrounds and bold ideas to push boundaries and help each other grow. Because full product development—from design to qualification to production—is within our team, we’re able to think differently, experiment more, and work quickly. Join us to power the future of the digital world.

This role will support a VP of Engineering and some of their Senior Director direct reports.

Your Impact

You will be extremely forward-thinking with a professional and approachable demeanor in all interactions; possess outstanding communication skills with all levels of staff, executives, customers, vendors; and good judgment.

• Calendar Management: Handles VP's calendar by prioritizing schedules and meetings. You may decide who gets on the principal’s calendar, which meetings are attended, and who can attend in their place.
• Event Speaking Engagement Coordination: Handles a running list of VP’s engagements and works closely with communications team to ensure content needs are understood and set in motion, so VP is prepared for each engagement.
• Meeting Planning and Organization: Assists VP in planning and organizing meetings by being responsible for the assembling of the agenda, location, meeting technology based upon participant needs, and all other meeting logistics. May further prepare meeting briefing documents by taking and disseminating notes and formulating post meeting action item list.
• Travel Briefing Preparation: Build travel packs for international trips as well as large domestic events such as Cisco Live, etc. This work includes combining all event information in addition to coordinated logistics of travel and customer/team asks.

Answers general questions as needed and refers routine matters to appropriate parties and follows up to ensure accurate completion. Takes the initiative to resolve issues within specified policies and guidelines and provides mentoring to administrative community members on problem solving. Figures out when executive action is required and supplies a recommendation where appropriate.
• Travel and Expense Management: Responsible for making in-depth global travel arrangements for VP. Carefully considers and decides the optimum travel arrangements and itinerary for calendared meetings while handling Cisco expenses. Works diligently to go above and beyond, working with the airlines directly to accommodate Global Services benefits for upgrades whenever they are available.
• Special Projects: Provides analytical support to assist executives on special projects. Research issues, analyzes problems, compiles data, and prepares reports.
• Large Corporate Events: Prepare and brief itinerary as well as accompany VP for large Corporate Events such as GSX, where EAs are used for executive support.
• Confidentiality: Candidate will deal professionally with sensitive and confidential matters and materials.

You have experience providing support at the VP level. You take initiative, can handle a full desk with ease and thrive in a lively environment. You have high-energy with a passion for thinking bigger and broader than the role itself. This position requires strong interpersonal skills, independent judgment, utmost integrity and ability to balance both strategic and tactical actions. You have outstanding attention to detail and the ability to handle confidential information. You enjoy a collaborative environment, are committed to improvement, solve problems and make decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

jobs.title: Head of CDO AI Strategy, Enablement and Delivery
jobs.description:
Wells Fargo is seeking a Head of AI Strategy, Enablement and Delivery for the Chief Data Office (CDO).

Responsibilities include:

• CDO AI Strategy: Define, publish, and continually refine the multi-year AI strategy and roadmap for the Chief Data Office, aligned to enterprise technology strategy, enterprise AI strategy, the Enterprise Data Strategy, and regulatory expectations.

• AI Enablement and Adoption: Build the enablement layer that allows lines of businesses to adopt AI on governed enterprise data, including reusable patterns, reference architectures, shared services, evaluation harnesses, and self-service tooling.

• AI Education and Adoption Series: Empower and equip CDO resources through an ongoing AI educational series that builds skills and confidence, improving adoption of AI tools across the data organization.

• Business Line Engagement: Engage executive sponsors, business unit leaders, and technology partners to identify and build high-impact AI opportunities, build consensus for investment, and drive literacy and change management that make adoption stick. Represents the Chief Data Office in enterprise investment and governance forums and builds consensus across peers without direct authority.

• Responsible AI: Align to enterprise standards for responsible AI, including model governance, bias mitigation, explainability, transparency, human oversight, and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.

• Risk and Regulatory Interface: Partner with Model Risk Management, Technology Risk, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, and Cybersecurity so that AI solutions are designed for control effectiveness and audit sustainability; Serves as the accountable leader for AI within CDO, including control design, issue remediation, and regulatory and audit engagement. Serves as the primary liaison to regulatory bodies (e.g., OCC, FRB) and to internal audit on AI matters and chairs the Chief Data Office AI forum with risk and governance partners.

• AI Risk Policy Adherence: Ensure adherence to Technology, Data, and Model Risk policies for all AI-developed use cases, from design through deployment and ongoing monitoring.

• Delivery Excellence: Oversee end-to-end execution of AI initiatives from ideation through production, partnering with the aligned technology team to set priorities and ensure successful technology capability development and deployment. Holds direct accountability for the availability, resilience, performance, and unit cost of the enterprise AI services owned by the Chief Data Office, including shared services provided to CDO and Data Domains, operating to defined service-level objectives.

• Platform Partnership: Partner with data platform, infrastructure, and technology operations teams so that AI workloads are supported by governed data, appropriate compute, and repeatable deployment and monitoring practices.

• Agentic AI Solutions: Drive the delivery of agentic AI solutions to govern enterprise data at scale, automating metadata, lineage, classification, data quality detection, and policy compliance.

• Measurement and Reporting: Define the metrics, KPIs, and measurement frameworks that quantify AI business impact in revenue growth, cost reduction, and risk mitigation, and report results to the Chief Data Officer and senior governance committees.

• Vendor and Financial Stewardship: Own the financial plan for the function, including approval of build, buy and partner decisions within a delegated authority, management of headcount, vendor spend, and consumption-based technology cost, and management of strategic partner relationships with performance and risk discipline.

• AI Tools and Token Cost Management: Own the inventory and management of AI tools for the Chief Data Office, and effectively manage token consumption and cost for the CDO division, including coordinating token forecasts with CXO partners.

• Talent and Leadership: Build and lead a multi-layer organization of AI product managers, and enablement specialists; mentor emerging leaders and foster a culture of accountability, experimentation, and excellence. Lead multiple sub-functions and geographies, including strategic vendor teams, and own the organizational design, location strategy, and succession plan for the function.

Alignment to the Enterprise Data Strategy

This role supports all three pillars of the Enterprise Data Strategy, making AI a force multiplier within each:

• Comprehensive Enterprise Data Governance: Apply AI and agentic solutions to govern data at scale, and ensure that AI data is itself governed, with models, prompts, agents, and training data inventoried, owned, monitored, and evidenced to regulator-ready standards.

• Data Strategy and Simplified Data Environments: Use AI to accelerate simplification through automated code and pipeline conversion, schema mapping, redundancy detection, and rationalization analysis, and standardize on enterprise AI patterns and platforms designed for reuse.

• Enhanced Analytic Capabilities: Extend analytics from descriptive reporting to predictive, generative, and agentic capability delivered on trusted data, equipping analytics and business teams to build safely within enterprise guardrails.

Critical Leadership Capabilities

• Strategic Thinking: Anticipates where AI capability and regulatory expectation are heading and positions the enterprise ahead of both; translates strategy into specific objectives and key results for units and individuals; provides board-level communication of efforts and progress.

• Driving Results: Delivery-oriented with a concentrated focus on quality for cornerstone capabilities; reviews performance and progress regularly, tests whether goals are sufficiently challenging, and implements corrective action based on deviations.

• Collaborating and Influencing: Strategically engages stakeholders across Technology, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and the lines of business to shape end-state designs; comfortable in front of large audiences, presenting a message clearly and succinctly to business, product, and executive leaders.

• Building People Capability: Serves as a talent magnet for the technology organization; grows followership of high-caliber talent, gives critical feedback in behavioral terms, and uses a regular assessment process to focus development effort.

Required Qualifications

• 10+ years of Technology Strategic Leadership experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education

• 4+ years of Management experience, including experience leading other people leaders.

• 8+ years of experience in data, analytics, or AI roles, including data management or data engineering.

• 5+ years of experience owning and driving roadmap strategy and definition for technology products or platforms.

• 4+ years of Risk Management, Business Controls, or Compliance experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education.

Desired Qualifications

• Demonstrated track record developing and executing AI or advanced analytics strategy at enterprise scale, including production deployment in cloud environments.

• Executive leadership experience in large, highly regulated financial services organizations, including regulatory and audit engagement.

• Experience leading the AI charter for a large technology or financial technology organization.

• Hands-on familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, and generative AI application patterns, and with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain, and LangGraph.

• Understanding of MLOps practices, model monitoring, and performance and cost tuning for AI workloads.

• Deep knowledge of AI governance and ethics, model risk management, privacy, and emerging AI regulation.

• Experience with data governance disciplines including metadata, lineage, data quality, and issue remediation.

• Experience operating in product-centric and agile delivery models, and with organizational design in large matrixed organizations.

• Proven ability to build and drive adoption of new tools and capabilities, and to lead globally distributed teams and strategic vendor partnerships.

• Advanced degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field.

Job Description:

Werkstudent*in (m/w/d) General Management – Fokus Transformation

Wir gestalten die Zukunft unserer Organisation und begleiten Veränderungsprozesse nachhaltig. Um unser Team bei strategischen Transformationsprojekten zu unterstützen, suchen wir ab sofort engagierte Verstärkung.

·       Workshop-Design & Moderation: Unterstützung bei der Vorbereitung und Durchführung von interaktiven Workshops, Change-Formaten und Trainings.

·       Recherche & Analyse: Eigenständige Recherche zu Best Practices, Trends im Bereich Change-Management, New Work und agilen Organisationsformen sowie Aufbereitung von Entscheidungsvorlagen.

·       Kommunikation & Change: Unterstützung bei der Erstellung von Change-Kommunikationsmaterialien (z. B. Präsentationen, Intranet-Beiträge, Newsletter).

jobs.title: Finance NextGen – Air Power Services Finance & Controlling (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Finance NextGen Programme(d/f/m)

The Finance NextGen Programme is an Airbus Defence & Space-wide development programme.This programme is designed to identify and develop talented Leaders for the Airbus Finance Community who will contribute significantly towards achieving our business goals. The Finance NextGen Programme - sponsored by Airbus Defence & Space' CFO - enables its participants to enhance financial know-how and expertise, combined with further learning in management and leadership competencies.

The mission of the programme:

Fostering and deepening participants’ financial knowledge and expertise on the Airbus world of Finance, enlarging the scope to the international financial context.

Linking formal learning with rotating, real-business project assignments.

Increasing participants’ project management and leadership competencies.

Encouraging networking, job shadowing, mobility and cross-cultural experiences.

Mentorship from a member of the Finance Top Management.

This Program consists of two assignments in two different countries. Each assignment lasts for a period of two years. They are combined with off-the-job modules, designed to strengthen participant’s management and financial competencies.

Your location

Located about an hour’s drive north of Munich, Manching is an up-and-coming market town that offers a wide range of leisure and cultural activities. Here, you can enjoy the quality of life in the countryside while the pleasures of near-by cities are still within easy reach.

Our Benefits for You

●     Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.

●     Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.

●     Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.

●     Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.

●     Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.

Your tasks and responsibilities

• Support all major financial planning processes as OP, FC, EAC.
• Support in the reporting of all Program relevant key data (e.g. P&L contribution, Balance Sheet, FCF, ...) and the related closing activities.
• Support in the preparation of the commercial part of bids (Costing and Pricing) and the related internal processes (e.g. RMC, ...) in accordance with German Price Law.
• Perform the financial contract execution within local ERP systems in accordance with the contract and local regulations and ensure cost transparency through continuous controlling.
• Challenge functions in terms of financial performance and drive further improvements.
• Perform invoicing activities to internal and external entities.
• Ensure adherence to financial principles and compliance.
• Perform external & internal invoicing including set-up of internal contract and support of purchase order and Purchase controlling.
